column3: The Hebrew makes dogs and birds the active eaters; BSB expresses their eating passively.
The Hebrew leaves the final striker and victim as pronouns; BSB supplies Baasha and the house of Jeroboam. It also describes the prophet’s mediation as “by the hand”.
The Hebrew leaves the drinking king unnamed and repeats Tirzah; BSB supplies Elah twice and uses “there” for the second Tirzah.
The Hebrew leaves the victim unnamed and the new king implicit; BSB names Elah and repeats Zimri.
The Hebrew leaves the new king unnamed and describes a male as one urinating against a wall; BSB supplies Zimri and uses “a single male”. It has plural kinsmen and singular friend.
The Hebrew explicitly says “by the hand” of Jehu; BSB leaves the hand implicit.
The Hebrew calls the idols “vanities”; BSB says “worthless idols”.
The Hebrew calls the encamped group “the people”; BSB has “the troops”.
The Hebrew calls Jeroboam’s example his “way”; BSB uses “example”.
The Hebrew says half followed Tibni “to make him king”; BSB has supporting him “as king”.
The Hebrew describes building the hill before separately naming the city he built; BSB first specifies building a city there.
The Hebrew uses singular “way” and “sin”; BSB uses plural “ways” and “sins”.
The Hebrew repeats Ahab son of Omri and reigning over Israel; BSB leaves both repetitions implicit.
